properties.Summary: Synthetic evidence suggests duplicate deliveries may explain some worker spend. The retry plan remains proposed; missing allocation and log coverage prevent a verified savings estimate.
properties.Next step: Confirm duplicate-delivery rate and cost allocation before choosing the retry change.

pages.content:
## Research question
What explains the synthetic worker cost increase, and would a retry change help?

## Context
Synthetic account alias research-dev; region us-west-2; Vantage workspace example; 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z to 2026-10-06T00:00:00Z; actual USD costs, daily granularity. Billing freshness and service allocation are incomplete.

## Findings
- Confirmed in synthetic fixtures: duplicate deliveries appear in a bounded log sample. Source: [Synthetic event sample](https://example.com/synthetic-event-sample), observed 2026-10-05, checked 2026-10-06. One page has a continuation token, so coverage is incomplete.
- Hypothesis, medium confidence: duplicate processing contributes to spend. [Synthetic cost report](https://example.com/synthetic-cost-report), observed 2026-10-05, checked 2026-10-06. Correlation alone does not establish attribution.

## Options and tradeoffs
Keep existing retries while measuring, or evaluate an idempotency guard after confirming the domain key. Savings are unverified.

## Takeaway
Measure delivery duplication and allocation before committing to a change. No implementation decision has been accepted.

## Proposed plan
1. Confirm the event identity contract. Complete when repeated deliveries can be matched without customer payloads.
2. Measure duplicate rate and attributable worker cost. Depends on step 1; complete when the date window and denominator match.
3. Compare the smallest safe change against current behavior. Depends on step 2; complete when behavior and failure checks are defined.

## Open questions
What is the duplicate rate outside the sample? How much spend belongs to this worker?

## Artifact
[Synthetic HTML explanation](https://example.com/synthetic-cost-brief.html) shows current and proposed flows. This example URL is illustrative; no upload or live visual review occurred.

## Sources
- [Synthetic cost report](https://example.com/synthetic-cost-report): actual USD costs; source date 2026-10-05; checked 2026-10-06; freshness/allocation incomplete.
- [Synthetic event sample](https://example.com/synthetic-event-sample): bounded UTC window; source date 2026-10-05; checked 2026-10-06; one page with continuation.

## Next step
Confirm duplicate-delivery rate and cost allocation before choosing the retry change.

## Dated updates
Capture ID: synthetic-cost-review-2026-10-06. This is a local synthetic fixture, not a live record.
